description: A talk of 12 turns: turn 1 (his son Luke is 14 and they read Greek on Sundays) has fallen out of the 10-turn window and is in `fold`, with an earlier summary; the answer to the ordinary question is plain, and carries the new summary that still names Luke and the age.

request.greek: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν τὸν θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν
request.english: And we know that all things work together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
request.question: And what does πρόθεσιν mean?

history.a: Οἴδαμεν is from οἶδα: 'we know'. It is first person plural, perfect in form, present in meaning.
δὲ is a small connecting word: 'and' or 'but', depending on the sentence.
ὅτι here introduces what we know: 'that'.
'Those who love', a present participle in the dative plural.
It says for whom all things work together: 'for those who love'.
'God', the object of the loving, in the accusative singular.
'Toward good': εἰς gives the direction the working together takes.

request.summary: He is learning Greek with his son. Earlier they covered the verse's first words.

fold.q: Before we start: my son Luke is 14 and we read Greek together on Sundays. What does ἀγαπῶσιν mean here?
fold.a: ἀγαπῶσιν is from ἀγαπάω, 'to love': 'those who love'. A good Sunday reading for you and Luke.
